record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Bell inequalities stronger than CHSH for Werner states
record.original_question: Find Bell inequalities stronger than the CHSH inequalities for Werner states, in the specific sense that the new inequalities are violated by a wider range of Werner states than CHSH is.

evidence.quote: Find Bell Inequalities which are stronger than the CHSH inequalities in the sense that they are violated by a wider range of Werner states.

Recently, Daniel Collins and Nicolas Gisin [CG] found a Bell Inequality and states which violate the new but not the CHSH inequalities. Alas, the range of Werner states violating the new inequality is smaller than that for the CHSH setting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a parameter $\lambda \in [-1,1]$, the two-qubit Werner state on $\mathbb{C}^2 \otimes \mathbb{C}^2$ is defined by
$$ho_\lambda \;=\; \lambda\, |\psi^-angle\langle\psi^-| \;+\;  rac{1-\lambda}{4}\, I_4,$$
where $|\psi^-angle = (|01angle - |10angle)/\sqrt{2}$ is the singlet state. (Equivalently, $ho_\lambda$ is the unique $U \otimes U$-invariant state with the given singlet fraction.)

The Clauser–Horne–Shimony–Holt (CHSH) inequality states that, for any local hidden-variable model with two dichotomic ($\pm 1$-valued) measurements per party, the quantity
$$\langle A_1 B_1angle + \langle A_1 B_2angle + \langle A_2 B_1angle - \langle A_2 B_2angle$$
is bounded in absolute value by $2$. The Werner state $ho_\lambda$ admits projective dichotomic measurements that violate this CHSH inequality if and only if $\lambda > 1/\sqrt{2}$.

Problem: Exhibit a Bell inequality (i.e. a linear inequality on joint correlations of finitely many local measurement outcomes that is valid for every local hidden-variable model) together with quantum measurements on $ho_\lambda$ such that the inequality is violated by $ho_\lambda$ for some value $\lambda \le 1/\sqrt{2}$. Equivalently, find a Bell inequality whose range of two-qubit Werner states $ho_\lambda$ exhibiting violation strictly contains the CHSH range $\lambda > 1/\sqrt{2}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is solved. Tamás Vértesi (2008, "More efficient Bell inequalities for Werner states", arXiv:0806.0096) constructed a family of Bell inequalities violated by two-qubit Werner states with visibility below the CHSH threshold $1/\sqrt{2}$, lowering the bound to about $0.7056$. Subsequent works have further improved this threshold.
